examples.en: I played the word chain game with my family in the car.

examples.ko: 끝말잇기 하다가 생각이 안 나서 졌어요.
examples.en: I couldn't think of a word during the word chain game, so I lost.

examples.ko: 끝말잇기가 한국어 단어 공부에 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: The word chain game helps with studying Korean words.
I killed boredom with the kids by playing the word chain game.

examples.ko: 끝말잇기에서 이기려면 단어를 많이 알아야 해요.
examples.en: To win at the word chain game, you need to know a lot of words.

examples.ko: 끝말잇기는 앞사람이 말한 단어의 마지막 글자로 시작해요.
examples.en: In the word chain game, you start with the last letter of the previous person's word.

explain: 앞사람이 말한 단어의 마지막 글자로 시작하는 단어를 차례로 말하는 말놀이예요. 친구나 가족과 이동하는 시간에 심심할 때 자주 해요. '끝말잇기를 하다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: I play the word chain game with friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀이를 한다고 말할 때 '하다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it with 하다 to say you play the game.

phrases.en: We played a word chain game on the bus.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 게임 makes it clearer that it is a game.

phrases.en: I won at the word chain game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이기고 지는 결과를 말할 때 '에서'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 에서 when talking about winning or losing.

explain_en: It is a word game in which each person says a word starting with the last syllable of the previous person's word. People often play it with friends or family when bored, such as during trips. You say '끝말잇기를 하다'.

examples.en: The doorkeeper let the child in.
Please send the patient into the ward.

examples.ko: 방에 신선한 공기를 들여보내려고 창문을 열었어요.
examples.en: I opened the window to let fresh air into the room.

examples.ko: 엄마가 아이를 먼저 집 안으로 들여보냈어요.
examples.en: Mom sent the child inside the house first.

examples.ko: 경비원은 신분증이 없는 사람은 안 들여보내요.
examples.en: The guard doesn't let in people without ID.

examples.ko: 시험장 안으로 학생들을 한 명씩 들여보내요.
examples.en: They send the students into the exam hall one by one.

explain: 사람이나 물건, 공기를 밖에서 안으로 보낼 때 써요. 반대말은 '내보내다'예요. 사람에게는 '들여보내 주다'로 말하면 들어가게 허락해 주는 느낌이 나요.

phrases.en: Please let the guest in first.
phrases.nuance_ko: '들여보내다'에 '주다'를 붙여 부탁하거나 허락할 때 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 주다 to 들여보내다 makes a polite request or permission to let someone in.

phrases.en: The teacher sent the students into the classroom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형이고 '안으로'를 붙여 들어간 방향을 분명히 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A past-tense form with 안으로 to make the direction inward clear.

phrases.en: If you don't have a ticket, they won't let you in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안으로 들어가지 못하게 할 때 쓰는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form used when people are not allowed to go inside.

explain_en: Use it for sending people, things or air from outside to inside. The opposite is '내보내다'. With people, '들여보내 주다' sounds like granting permission to enter.

examples.en: I separate the trash by type.
Separate paper and plastic before throwing them out.
Let's think about the two problems separately.
We separated the students by class.

examples.ko: 일과 생활을 분리하는 게 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It is not easy to separate work from life.

examples.ko: 이 부분은 손으로 분리할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can take this part off by hand.

explain: '분리수거', '분리배출'처럼 쓰레기를 버릴 때 가장 자주 들어요. '나누다'는 몫을 가르거나 이야기를 '나누다'처럼 폭이 넓고, '분리하다'는 붙어 있던 것을 떼어 놓는 느낌이에요. 반대말은 '합치다', '결합하다'예요.

phrases.en: I do recycling sorting every Sunday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓰레기를 종류별로 나눠서 버리는 일을 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for sorting trash by type for disposal.

phrases.en: Please tell me how to sort my waste.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문이나 뉴스에서 자주 쓰는, 조금 더 격식 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A slightly more formal term seen in notices and the news.

phrases.en: I take the cap off the bottle and throw it away separately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 붙어 있는 부분을 떼어 낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when detaching a part that is attached.

explain_en: You hear it most often with trash, as in 분리수거 and 분리배출. 나누다 is broad, covering splitting shares or 'sharing' a talk, while 분리하다 feels like pulling apart things that were attached. The opposites are 합치다 and 결합하다.

examples.en: I made a promise with my friend by hooking little fingers.
I put a bandage on my hurt little finger.
My little finger got caught in the door and swelled up.

examples.ko: 기타를 칠 때는 새끼손가락까지 써야 해요.
examples.en: When playing guitar, you have to use even your little finger.
Only my little finger wouldn't straighten, so I went to the hospital.
Let's hook little fingers and make a firm promise.

explain: '새끼손가락을 걸다'는 약속할 때 하는 행동이라서 한국에서 아이들 사이에서 많이 해요. 다른 손가락은 '엄지', '검지', '중지', '약지'라고 하고, 마지막 손가락만 '새끼손가락'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 그녀는 새끼손가락에 작은 반지를 끼고 있어요.
phrases.en: She wears a small ring on her little finger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반지를 어느 손가락에 끼는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say which finger a ring is worn on.
phrases.en_equiv: to wear a ring on the little finger

phrases.en: I hurt my little finger by getting it caught in the door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손가락을 다쳤을 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrase for injuring the little finger.

phrases.en: That bug is about the size of a little finger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 것의 크기를 새끼손가락에 비교해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the size of a small thing by comparing it to a little finger.
phrases.en_equiv: about the size of a little finger

explain_en: '새끼손가락을 걸다' (hooking pinkies) is a gesture used when promising, and it is very common among Korean children. The other fingers are '엄지', '검지', '중지' and '약지', and only the last one is '새끼손가락'.

examples.en: The children are happily playing tag in the park.
I fell while playing tag and hurt my knee.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 동네 친구들과 술래잡기를 자주 했어요.
examples.en: As a child, I often played tag with the neighborhood kids.

examples.ko: 오늘은 술래잡기 말고 다른 놀이를 해요.
examples.en: Let's play a different game today instead of tag.

examples.ko: 술래잡기에서는 잡힌 사람이 다음 술래가 돼요.
examples.en: In tag, the person who gets caught becomes the next "it."
Shall we all play tag together?

explain: 원래는 술래가 숨은 사람을 찾는 놀이라서 '숨바꼭질'과 같은 말이에요. 요즘은 술래가 쫓아가서 잡는 놀이도 술래잡기라고 해요. '술래잡기하다'처럼 동사로도 써요.

phrases.en: The kids play tag in the yard.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun used as a verb with 하다.

phrases.nuance_ko: 숨은 사람을 찾는 놀이만 가리킬 때는 이 말이 더 정확해요.
phrases.nuance_en: More exact when you mean only the game of finding hidden people.

phrases.en: Let's play tag together in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀이라는 점을 분명히 말하고 싶을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to make clear that it is a game.

explain_en: Originally it is the game where the seeker looks for hidden people, so it means the same as '숨바꼭질'. These days it also refers to a game where the chaser runs after and catches others. It also works as a verb, as in '술래잡기하다'.

examples.en: We drew lots to divide the work fairly.
To be fair, we decided the seats by drawing lots.
I drew number one in the lottery draw.
Drawing lots is fair because it's the same no matter who draws.
We shared the year-end party gifts by drawing lots.
The children lined up in the order they drew.

explain: 가위바위보나 사다리타기처럼 운으로 정할 때 쓰는 방법이에요. '제비를 뽑다'라고도 하고, '제비뽑기로 정하다'처럼 방법을 말할 때 '-로'와 자주 써요.

phrases.en: Everyone drew lots to decide the order.
phrases.nuance_ko: '제비뽑기를 하다'와 같은 뜻인데, 종이를 하나 뽑는 동작에 초점을 둬요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the same as doing a lottery, but focuses on the act of picking one slip.

phrases.en: I was chosen in the drawing of lots.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결과를 말할 때 써요. 당첨된 사람이 주어가 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the result, with the chosen person as the subject.

phrases.en: We decide who does the cleaning duty by drawing lots.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방법을 말할 때 '-로'와 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with '-로' to name the method of deciding.

explain_en: It is a way to decide by luck, like rock-paper-scissors or ladder drawing. You can also say '제비를 뽑다', and '제비뽑기로 정하다' with '-로' is a common way to state the method.
